one_line: A Robert's Rules clerk's bench whose live WebMCP tool surface encodes the meeting's currently legal motions.
what_it_does: Tracks parliamentary motion state, dynamically exposes only motions that are in order, plans contingent paths, and drafts minutes while treating quoted content as untrusted data.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product's central mechanism: the available action surface itself is the legal motion state, so an agent cannot call an out-of-order motion rather than merely receiving a refusal. Shared live state and dynamic registration materially change reliability and safety beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says getTools() renders the current in-order motion set and an out-of-order motion is absent, not refused.
Changing members present from 7 to 4 collapses the tool surface from 17 to 9 without changing phase.
explain_path_to performs an AND-OR search over uncontrolled vote outcomes and returns a proved plan.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually coherent end-to-end evidence of the motion stack, quorum changes, planning, and injection-resistant minutes, with a live demo and video. Small details are still claimed through transcript rather than independently inspectable source here.
execution_evidence: 158-second video is supplied with a transcript covering multiple complete states.
Transcript reports 399-node depth-6 planning, dynamic tool removal, and minutes that preserve an injected string as data while leaving the motion pending.
Demo is marked alive and the project has a public repository.
impact_rationale: Small boards, associations, student unions, and nonprofits have a concrete procedural problem and often lack parliamentarians; the product directly reduces procedural mistakes and makes state legible.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies homeowners' associations, co-op boards, student unions, and small nonprofits as intended users.
The demonstrated workflow handles amendments, quorum, voting contingencies, and minutes rather than generic meeting notes.
creativity_rationale: It turns a formal rule system into a capability surface: legal procedure becomes the agent's available vocabulary, combined with contingent planning and prompt-injection-resistant recordkeeping.
creativity_evidence: The core concept is that an out-of-order motion does not exist to be called.
The motion stack, dynamic tool registration, AND-OR outcome planning, and contradictory minute record form a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: The clerk-oriented two-column state view and explicit rule explanations appear highly legible for a specialized workflow.
standouts: Capability surface is itself a semantic model of parliamentary legality.
Strong safety treatment of quorum changes and untrusted motion text.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with strong demonstrated execution, impact, and originality.

one_line: A local exam-practice workspace where a user's existing AI agent creates tests and feedback alongside saved attempts.
what_it_does: Provides IELTS, SAT, GRE, and custom practice in a timed exam interface, saves attempts locally, scores objective answers, and attaches agent feedback to exact submissions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to create tests, read attempts, and save feedback in the same local workspace, with validation and attempt identity. A general agent could drive much of the UI, but reliable state linkage adds meaningful value.
leverage_evidence: About text names tools for adding practice tests, reading completed attempts, and saving feedback.
The app and tools share commands, with Zod validation and recoverability on failed saves.
Frame sheet visibly shows completed listening/writing states, submission confirmation, review, and updated practice history, but not readable tool calls.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent learning loop and the frame sheet shows a substantial completion/submission/review flow. WebMCP end-to-end invocation is not visibly proven, limiting confidence and the score.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows listening completion, writing submission confirmation, writing completion, feedback/review, and return to practice history.
Demo is marked alive and a public repository is listed.
No submitted video and no clearly readable WebMCP invocation panel are available.
impact_rationale: Learners preparing for common exams have a clear need for practice and targeted feedback; using an existing AI subscription lowers the barrier to an iterative study loop.
impact_evidence: Packet explicitly targets IELTS, SAT, GRE, and custom subject practice.
The demonstrated workflow links timed tests, saved attempts, and written feedback.
creativity_rationale: The bring-your-own-agent exam workspace is a useful new angle on a known test-prep category, but the core practice and feedback model is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates inside the exam environment and feedback is tied to exact attempts.
Concept remains a conventional exam-prep workflow with an agent integration.
usability_note: Visible completion, confirmation, history, and review states suggest a clear learner flow.
red_flags: No video; frame sheets do not clearly expose WebMCP calls.
standouts: Local-first attempt continuity and feedback linkage.
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and a coherent product loop; WebMCP evidence is thinner than the concept claims.

one_line: A human-approved survey research workspace where agents draft, target, publish, monitor, and analyze studies.
what_it_does: Combines survey creation and distribution with structured agent assistance, approval gates for consequential actions, monitoring, subgroup analysis, and saved analysis views.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate across a multi-step research workflow while humans approve publication and other consequential actions. Structured tools and shared state are materially safer and more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text lists context review, survey drafting, targeting, approval before publishing, monitoring, analysis, subgroup comparison, and export preparation.
Explicit human approval is required before publishing.
Nine gallery images and an alive demo are listed, though no video is submitted.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packet describes a complete research lifecycle, but the evidence is primarily narrative and packaging; the central agent workflow is not visually demonstrated end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text specifies the workflow and safety boundary in detail.
Public repository and alive demo are listed.
No video and no frame sheets with legible tool activity were available.
impact_rationale: Researchers and campus communities have a concrete need for accessible survey distribution and analysis; approval-gated automation plausibly improves throughput without removing human responsibility.
impact_evidence: Packet names campus researchers, respondents, survey publishers, and research-analysis use cases.
The product addresses design through analysis rather than only survey drafting.
creativity_rationale: Human-plus-agent research operations with explicit approval gates are a fresh synthesis, though survey platforms and agent workflow automation are established categories.
creativity_evidence: Agent is positioned as a collaborator inside the research platform, not a chatbot beside it.
Approval before publishing and saved analysis views deepen the interaction model.
usability_note: The explicit approval boundary is reassuring, but login and a broad workflow may create onboarding complexity.
red_flags: Competition additions are described, but the packet does not independently demonstrate them end-to-end.
standouts: Consequential-action approval is integrated into the research workflow.
advance_reason: Credible and high-impact workflow with strong leverage, pending deeper observed execution evidence.

one_line: A command center bundling six agent-drivable applications behind shared human/agent controls.
what_it_does: Hosts a kanban board, restaurant picker, policy diff, resume gap finder, ambient note taker, and illustrated chapter reader, each exposing the same page actions to humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP unifies six distinct interfaces under a shared, discoverable, same-screen control model and human confirmations. The individual tasks remain largely UI-automatable, so the delta is meaningful but not transformative.
leverage_evidence: About text reports 44 page tools, shared button/function implementations, and an Agent is driving indicator.
Destructive actions wait for an in-page confirmation.
The packet reports an alive demo and public repository but no video.
execution_rationale: The breadth is ambitious and the architecture is coherent, but the packet provides little observed evidence of the six workflows or agent calls beyond the narrative and one gallery image.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates six concrete applications and a shared registration hook.
WebMCP catalog is rendered from the same definitions used by pages.
No video and only one gallery image are listed.
impact_rationale: The constituent tools address recognizable productivity, decision, career, and creative needs, though the bundle's audience and value proposition are diffuse.
impact_evidence: Six named applications cover concrete everyday and professional tasks.
Human confirmation and no API-key access for tools reduce operational risk.
creativity_rationale: Packaging six varied agent-driven builds into one command center and preserving the same surface for human and agent interaction is an ambitious, memorable synthesis.
creativity_evidence: One command center spans kanban, group choice, policy analysis, career planning, notes, and visual reading.
The shared WebMCP hook and page-local tool catalogs create a coherent meta-product.
usability_note: A single command center can reduce switching, but six product modes may dilute focus.
red_flags: Most constituent builds predate the challenge, according to the packet.
No video means the broad execution claim is not strongly observed.
standouts: Ambitious multi-app WebMCP surface with consistent human confirmation.
advance_reason: Creative breadth and credible shared architecture merit advancement despite thin observed evidence.

one_line: An agent-ready search and discovery layer that exposes storefront product search through MCP and WebMCP.
what_it_does: Adds structured product discovery tools to ecommerce sites so agents can search and help shoppers without merchants rebuilding their storefronts.
leverage_rationale: Structured browser tools can make product discovery more reliable than scraping and keep the agent on the same catalog experience as the shopper, but the packet shows little detail about the actual tool surface or workflow.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts explicit structured actions with scraping buttons and product information.
It claims WebMCP tools on participating storefronts and an ecommerce search layer.

execution_rationale: The architecture and purpose are plausible, but evidence is mostly a short pitch and architecture/demo image references; central product behavior is not demonstrated sufficiently.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive.
About text describes the integration approach and target workflow.
No public repository, video, or submitted frame sheets are listed.

impact_evidence: Packet identifies ecommerce merchants and shoppers as the intended parties.
The solution directly addresses agent access to search and product context.
creativity_rationale: Agent-ready ecommerce search is timely and useful but is a familiar application of structured tools, with limited evidence of a distinctive interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Bridges normal storefront UX and agent discovery without replatforming.
No novel interaction details are substantiated in the packet.
usability_note: The proposition is simple for merchants conceptually, but API-key access and participating-storefront integration imply setup friction.
red_flags: Sparse evidence: no repo, video, or frame sheets; project origin is not established.
advance_reason: Promising impact and reasonable leverage, but execution and eligibility evidence are too thin.

one_line: A deterministic airline-disruption simulator where the available WebMCP capabilities change with operational state and authority.
what_it_does: Checks schedules and plans recovery, then conditionally exposes cancellation and commit tools through drafting, legality, approval, and committed states.
leverage_rationale: The core product question is when a capability should exist. State-governed registration makes authority boundaries discoverable and enforceable at the agent surface, rather than relying on refusals after invocation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists six operational states and seven tools whose availability changes across them.
cancel_flight appears only when required; commit_recovery_plan appears only after a legal draft and approval.
The pitch explicitly distinguishes proposal, website decision, and human commit.
execution_rationale: The state machine and safety model are clearly specified and the packet includes six gallery images, but no video or direct invocation evidence limits observed end-to-end credit.
execution_evidence: About text gives a deterministic scenario and explicit state progression.
Demo is marked alive and repository is public.
No submitted video; evidence is narrative plus gallery packaging.
impact_rationale: Airline operations are a concrete high-stakes planning domain, and the authority separation generalizes to other workflows; the fictional simulation limits direct operational impact.
impact_evidence: Scenario includes aircraft position, crew duty, turn time, disruption window, and human approval.
The concept explicitly targets high-stakes workflows beyond aviation.
creativity_rationale: Treating tool registration as a dynamic authority firewall and making the state machine visible is a strong, memorable interaction concept with clear depth.
creativity_evidence: The agent's capabilities evolve from disruption through drafting, cancellation-required, legal draft, approval, and committed states.
The product emphasizes nonexistence rather than refusal as the safety primitive.
usability_note: The staged authority model should be understandable in the simulator, though state transitions may be complex for casual users.
red_flags: No video means the described transitions are not independently observed.
standouts: Very clear capability-lifecycle thesis with high-stakes relevance.
advance_reason: One of the strongest WebMCP-native concepts, with unusually clear state-governed authority boundaries.

one_line: A parametric 3D pottery-template editor that lets an agent explore shape while the app deterministically exports printable geometry.
what_it_does: Pairs an AI agent to a browser editor, applies reversible parameter changes, unfolds 3D vessels into multi-page clay templates, and exports precise PDFs.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP/paired browser control lets the agent handle difficult design iteration while deterministic app geometry guarantees a usable printable output; undo/redo and shared state make the collaboration materially better than agent-generated PDFs.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript shows an agent changing parameters in a paired browser and the result arriving in under a second via WebSocket.
Transcript emphasizes deterministic multipage templates and reversible human/agent changes.
Frames and about text show the 3D editor and exported printable PDF template.
execution_rationale: The 179-second video demonstrates pairing, agent-driven edits, a responsive editor, and export-oriented geometry; the exact WebMCP/polyfill architecture is somewhat nonstandard but the workflow is coherent.
execution_evidence: Video is supplied with a transcript describing a complete edit-and-sync flow.
Gallery includes editor, tool availability, dark/light modes, and multipage PDF output.
Demo is alive.
impact_rationale: Potters and makers have a concrete pain point: AI-generated templates can be inconsistent or fail after hours of physical work. Deterministic printable output directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: About text describes cereal-box template making, misaligned PDFs, and studio time lost to failures.
Output is explicitly a multipage template true to the built 3D shape.
creativity_rationale: The division of labor—agent handles unusual geometric intent while the deterministic editor handles fabrication truth—is a compelling and original creative-tool interaction.
creativity_evidence: Pairs conversational AI design with parametric unfolding and reversible browser state.
The product is aimed at physical craft output, not merely a visual 3D mockup.
usability_note: Human-editable parameters, pairing, undo/redo, and deterministic export support a strong collaborative workflow, though pairing adds setup.
red_flags: Implementation uses a paired-browser/WebSocket bridge and a polyfill path, so the exact native WebMCP boundary is less direct than the pitch suggests.
standouts: Clear human/agent division of labor tied to real-world fabrication reliability.
Strong visual and video evidence of the central workflow.
advance_reason: Excellent creative and practical use of agent collaboration with strong end-to-end evidence.

one_line: A browser-local capability firewall that lets agents analyze private tab data without receiving the underlying records.
what_it_does: Loads CSV data locally, exposes aggregate/profile/query/chart/audit tools according to a trust dial, enforces group-size thresholds, and records released information in an egress ledger.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the security boundary: changing policy unregisters tools so stale handles fail with tool nonexistence, while computation stays in the browser. Generic UI automation cannot provide the same capability-lifecycle semantics as cleanly.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript explicitly shows a tool being unregistered after the trust dial changes and a subsequent NotFoundError.
Data remains local, with connect-src 'none' and aggregate thresholds.
The exposed tool surface is governed live by policy rather than post-call refusal.
execution_rationale: The 130-second video demonstrates the main trust-dial, stale-tool, local-data, and egress-ledger flow, and the written description fills in the security design coherently.
execution_evidence: Video is supplied and transcript covers discovery, capability withdrawal, stale invocation failure, and local analysis.
Public repo and alive demo are listed.
About text gives concrete local/released byte ledger values and up to eleven tools.
impact_rationale: Organizations and individuals handling payroll, patient, customer, or unreleased financial data have a real privacy constraint; useful analysis without uploading records is a credible high-value solution.
impact_evidence: Packet names concrete sensitive datasets and NDA/data-egress contexts.
Minimum group-size aggregation and an egress ledger address privacy risk directly.
creativity_rationale: The capability-firewall framing, live policy-controlled registration, stale-handle nonexistence, and local-only computation form an original and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product closes capability ports rather than asking a model to obey a refusal.
It combines privacy-preserving local analysis with an auditable release ledger.
usability_note: The trust dial and egress ledger make policy legible, though privacy controls and aggregate semantics may require expert understanding.
standouts: Exceptional alignment between WebMCP semantics and the product's security thesis.
advance_reason: Outstanding WebMCP leverage, strong proof, major privacy impact, and a distinctive concept.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes a rich structured canvas API and lets the agent build incrementally in shared visible state, which is more precise and collaborative than generic clicking or batch image generation.
leverage_evidence: About text reports 32 tools covering canvas primitives and scene/layout operations.
Agent actions update the same canvas with reveal animations while humans watch and can undo.
A layout engine turns semantic scene requests into positioned diagrams.

execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo are listed.
About text specifies React/SVG implementation, registration, layout modes, and undo.
No submitted video and no gallery images are listed.
impact_rationale: Teams, students, educators, and presenters can benefit from real-time diagramming and iterative visual explanation; the shared canvas is a credible collaboration improvement.
impact_evidence: The product supports common diagram types, equations, code blocks, and illustrations.
It addresses the limitation of batch/static AI diagram tools.
creativity_rationale: The live, step-by-step agent drawing model and semantic layout engine are a fresh synthesis beyond static diagram generation.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent work on the same canvas with visible incremental drawing.
Four-level visual fallback and multiple structured layout modes deepen the concept.

standouts: Strong shared-state visual interaction and semantic layout abstraction.

one_line: A browser studio where an agent authors fictional coding-agent sessions that render as controllable SVG/video scenes.
what_it_does: Lets agents load and patch scripts, set camera and themes, inspect timelines, capture frames, request approval, and export deterministic animated SVG/CSS scenes.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on the actual stage and can inspect facts unavailable from a static prompt, while human approval gates rewrites and export. Structured tools improve repeatability and precise scene control.
leverage_evidence: Transcript reports the agent reading the guide, loading a script, operating a choice and voice-input step, setting theme/camera, inspecting calls, and exporting.
About text lists load_script, direct_camera, inspect_timeline, snapshot_frame, fit_duration, propose_patch, approval, and export tools.
The rail shows every call and the script preserves every visible string.
execution_rationale: The 170-second video describes and visibly sequences authoring, rendering, interaction, camera/theme changes, terminal surface, approval, and export; the product scope is unusually complete.
execution_evidence: Video and detailed transcript cover a complete studio workflow across app and terminal surfaces.
Demo is alive and repository is public.
Export output is specified as animated SVG with CSS keyframes and no JavaScript.
impact_rationale: Documentation authors, presenters, and developers have a real need for reproducible, secret-free coding-agent session visuals; the value is specific though niche.
impact_evidence: About text identifies READMEs, docs, talks, and posts as use cases.
Fictional/re-shootable sessions avoid leaking secrets and support translation and repeatability.
creativity_rationale: Treating an agent session as a scriptable stage with approvals, choices, timing inspection, camera, and deterministic export is a highly original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product renders fictional coding-agent sessions rather than merely recording real ones.
It combines inspectable timeline facts, voice/choice beats, direct scene control, and export safety.
usability_note: Approval cards, visible call rail, undo, and a complete authoring guide support control, although the studio is aimed at technically sophisticated users.
standouts: Agent edits the real stage and can query deterministic visual/timing facts.
Strong approval and privacy defaults for generated session media.
advance_reason: Distinctive, deeply pursued creative tool with strong video proof and meaningful WebMCP leverage.
